title: Documenting Sustainability and Legacy in Sport: A Comparative Analysis of Voga&Share and Paris 2024
content: Sport is increasingly associated with sustainability and legacy objectives, although documentary commitments do not necessarily establish achieved effects. This study compared how sustainability- and legacy-related content was documented in Voga&Share, an Erasmus+ community-oriented rowing initiative, and the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with attention to the Marseille sailing-host context. A comparative qualitative document analysis was conducted using a corpus of 15 English-language documents: six relating to Voga&Share and nine to Paris 2024. Documents were converted into page-level records and screened deductively across governance; environment; health and inclusion; economy and heritage; and monitoring and evidence. Match frequencies were normalised per 1,000 words, and six high-density extracts were manually coded to distinguish claim types and evidence status. Paris 2024 showed a higher overall density of thematic matches (53.3 per 1,000 words) than Voga&Share (34.4). Monitoring and evidence was the most frequent dimension in Paris 2024 (12.4 per 1,000 words), whereas health and inclusion predominated in Voga&Share (13.5). Pilot coding identified strategic commitments, implemented activities and reported outputs, but did not independently demonstrate achieved outcomes. The findings indicate contrasting documentary profiles shaped by organisational scale, institutional setting, document type and reporting purpose. Documentary analysis can clarify priorities and reported actions, but it cannot establish causality, additionality or durable sustainability legacy.
